headline: More than 100 members of Congress have asked Google and the defunct Spirit Airlines to halt a $10 million sale of the airline's internal data for training Google's AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large lawmaker letter on worker privacy in AI training data, but it is a request, not a legal action, and no decision on the deal is reported.
importance_line: Former Spirit employees' emails, chat messages and payroll records could be used to train AI, and lawmakers argue that stripping names may not protect them, but Google disputes that personal data is involved and no regulator has stopped the deal.
summary: The Record reports that 114 federal lawmakers, led by Rep. Steven Horsford and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, wrote to the chief executives of Google and Spirit Airlines on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 urging them to halt a deal in which Google would pay $10 million for Spirit's internal data, which Horsford says includes about 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages and payroll and tax records. Google says it is 'not looking to buy any personal information' and that an independent third party will exclude or de-identify the data first, but the lawmakers warn that removing names and email addresses does not necessarily make data anonymous when used with modern AI.
notes: Reuters original (listed in the pool) returned HTTP 401; text read on The Record (Recorded Future News), which did its own reporting from the press release and letter. Reuters/Economic Times summary says 'more than 120' lawmakers; The Record says 114 signed; The Record's figure is used. Spirit's shutdown was announced in May 2026 per The Record.
